title: Inverse counit comparisons preserve composition and naturality
statement: Let Q_i:C_i→D_i be functors, Tp,Tq,Tr the underived maps, Dp,Dq,Dr their derived analogues, κ:Tp⋙Tq≅Tr and c:Dp⋙Dq≅Dr. Let εp,εq,εr be natural counits and θp,θq,θr invertible model comparisons with μ the model reassociation. Assume the composite counit equation and the underived model pasting equation, and invertibility of the three counits at the specified models. Then the localized model inverses followed by the inverse counits obey the derived composition equation. Conjugation by natural chart isomorphisms preserves this equation and naturality. Between objects at which a natural counit is invertible, its inverse is natural; composing with a natural model comparison remains natural.

source.place: Elementary naturality and cancellation in the universal-property proof of Tag 0D5S, and affine chart transport in Tag 08DW.

proof.text: Postcompose the proposed derived composition equality by the direct counit and use its invertibility to cancel. Substitute the composite counit equation; cancel the first inverse counit, use naturality to move the model isomorphism through the second counit, and cancel the second inverse counit. The remaining equality is localization of the inverse underived model equation.

For chart conjugation cancel the adjacent middle-chart inverse factors, move the initial chart through c by naturality, and move the final chart through μ. This yields the already proved un-conjugated equation.

For naturality postcompose by an invertible counit, substitute the counit naturality square and cancel its inverse. Apply naturality of the model and chart isomorphisms to obtain the two extended naturality lemmas.
